Details
  • Original code: https://github.com/huggingface/pytorch-image-models at 0df212b369a5
  • Code licence: Apache-2.0 (permissive); files:
  • Weights licence: LicenseRef-Apple-Sample-Code
  • Licence evidence: https://huggingface.co/timm/fastvit_sa24.apple_dist_in1k/blob/0b86f2b98f83274e9f03b6ddbcb3942b84efb839/README.md
  • Training data: ImageNet-1k (ILSVRC 2012 classification)
  • Licence note: The weights are under Apple's sample-code licence (the timm Hugging Face card says only 'license: other'); that licence grants no patent rights.
  • Kernel libraries: cudnn_hacc, fvm_conv, fvm_extra, fvm_mb, fvm_r3
  • Variants: fastvit_sa24.apple_dist_in1k (default of fastvit_sa24)
  • Outputs: logits; label_set: imagenet-1k
  • Input size: fixed 256x256: the input is resized (short side 284) and centre-cropped to it
  • Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): fastvit_sa24.apple_dist_in1k 256x256 (0.1 GiB peak allocated, 0.1 reserved)
  • fastvit_sa24.apple_dist_in1k 224x224, first call: portable + torch.compile 9 s (cold Inductor cache), TensorRT fp16 45 s (ONNX + engine).
  • fastvit_sa24.apple_dist_in1k original 224x224: torch.autocast(fp16) around the forward
  • fastvit_sa24.apple_dist_in1k load / first call: original 2.49 s / 1.669 s, portable 0.62 s / 0.17 s, kernels 2.42 s / 0.048 s
  • Protocol, median of 9 after 3 warm-up, uint8 CUDA input (synthetic for bench_inputs sizes), card defaults; gc before each load; peak = max over the first call and the timed calls

Measured

fastforks: the model's own resize / crop on the GPU; original: the library's pretrained loader and its PIL eval transform. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.
